retainedFailures.reason: New history parameter too similar to content; renamed locally
Two fixture option branches needed map_or_else; corrected without weakening checks

notes: New ContextItem AssistantToolCalls and ToolCallResult preserve original call IDs, order, parameters, result and failure state; legacy text variants remain readable
Native checkpoints store explicit typed metadata matching canonical message content and role; ordinary model text is never parsed as a tool call, and malformed/orphan metadata is refused
Serialized typed content participates in existing message/token budgets, with the existing 1-MiB message bound; compaction removes metadata for removed messages
Native runtime generation now passes structured SDK messages through the selected provider rather than flattening them into a user prompt or synthesizing tool result IDs
This native path uses persistent context as its history authority and does not duplicate HTTP adapter history; unmatched or unanswered calls fail before inference
Legacy tool output, retrieved records and summaries are data-role messages instead of system instructions; host rules and current goals keep their system role

The existing actual model-memory fixture runs Chat, Responses and Anthropic, verifies original call IDs in second-round wire fields, bound approval and separate-device notes with six inference requests per mode
Existing LRU context test now closes and reopens redb, validating restored typed calls/results and explicit reset
The first role test used an orphan tool entry before the first user turn; it was corrected to actual conversation order without changing truncation rules
New readers accept old checkpoints without typed metadata. Downgrading to older closed-schema readers after writing the new field is not claimed compatible
No dependency changes/downloads, real accounts, production proxy/process changes, browser execution, device migration, deployment or Git writes
unverified: Recovery UX for incomplete historical tool groups: these currently fail before a new provider request rather than inventing missing results
Opaque/signed reasoning replay, all third-party context engines and actual provider-account acceptance
Role separation is not proof that a model resists all prompt injection; tool authority/approval remains mandatory
Runtime usage/finish/cost durability, both earlier native-credential anomalies and whole-project acceptance
